sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A LARGE UPPER TROUGH OVER THE WRN CONUS IS FORECAST TO BECOME SLIGHTLY MORE PROGRESSIVE LATE IN THE D1 PERIOD AS A VORTICITY MAXIMA PIVOTS THROUGH ITS BASE. IN THE MEANTIME...A BROAD AREA OF SWLY UPPER-LEVEL FLOW WILL BE PRESENT DOWNSTREAM ACROSS THE SRN ROCKIES INTO THE CNTRL/NRN PLAINS AND UPPER MS VALLEY. MINOR MIDLEVEL VORTICITY MAXIMA WILL BE EMBEDDED WITHIN THIS FLOW REGIME...AND WILL LIKELY INFLUENCE TO SOME DEGREE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT LATER IN THE AFTERNOON. AT THE SURFACE...A LOW-LEVEL BAROCLINIC ZONE WILL EXTEND SWD ACROSS THE ERN DAKOTAS AND THEN SWWD TOWARD AN AREA OF LOW PRESSURE OVER THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS. A SURFACE TROUGH/DRYLINE WILL EXTEND SSWWD FROM THE LOW INTO ERN NM/FAR W TX. SWLY FLOW ALOFT WILL MAINTAIN AN EML OVER THE PLAINS...WITH A SLY LOW-LEVEL JET EXTENDING NWD FROM THE SRN HIGH PLAINS INTO ERN NEB. ELSEWHERE...A WEAK MIDLEVEL ANTICYCLONE WILL RESIDE OVER THE SERN CONUS...WITH A RIDGE OF SURFACE HIGH PRESSURE LOCATED BENEATH THIS FEATURE SHUNTING RICHER LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE TO THE ATLANTIC AND GULF COASTS.

sections.title: N-CNTRL HIGH PLAINS TO THE UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: GIVEN VERY LITTLE CHANGE IS FORECAST TO OCCUR IN THE LARGE-SCALE FLOW REGIME DURING MUCH OF THE DAY...GREATEST CONCENTRATION OF SVR IS EXPECTED TO OCCUR INVOF A LOW-LEVEL BAROCLINIC ZONE ORIENTED NE-SW FROM NERN SD INTO WRN NEB. UPPER 60S DEWPOINTS WILL RESIDE ALONG THE FRONTAL ZONE OVER ERN SD/NEB...WHILE UPSLOPE ENELY FLOW AIDS IN MAINTAINING 40S AND 50S DEWPOINTS OVER THE N-CNTRL HIGH PLAINS. STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL ONCE AGAIN BE PRESENT ACROSS THE REGION...WHICH WILL CONTRIBUTE TOWARD STRONG TO EXTREME INSTABILITY FROM THE DAKOTAS SWD INTO NEB. STORMS WILL BE ONGOING OVER THE UPPER MS VALLEY/UPPER MIDWEST AT THE START OF THE PERIOD...AS WELL AS WRN/CNTRL SD INTO SERN MT. SOME OF THIS ACTIVITY WILL POSE A THREAT FOR ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS DURING THE MORNING...BUT MAY WEAKEN TOWARD MIDDAY. BY AFTERNOON...ADDITIONAL THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IS LIKELY OVER THE HIGH PLAINS WITHIN THE UPSLOPE FLOW REGIME. STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AND LONG/STRAIGHT HODOGRAPHS WILL FAVOR SUPERCELLS AND A LARGE HAIL THREAT. FARTHER E FROM WRN NEB INTO CNTRL/ERN SD...A COMBINATION OF LOW-LEVEL FRONTOGENESIS AND MINOR MIDLEVEL IMPULSES MOVING ACROSS THE AREA WILL LEAD TO SCATTERE

sections.title: SRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: A SURFACE TROUGH/DRYLINE WILL EXTEND SWWD FROM ERN CO INTO ERN NM AND FAR W TX THIS AFTERNOON...WITH SURFACE DEWPOINTS IN THE 50S EXPECTED TO RESIDE E OF THE TROUGH. TEMPERATURES WARMING INTO THE 90S WILL AID IN WEAK TO MODERATE MLCAPE VALUES AND ALSO CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES. BY LATE AFTERNOON...MULTICELL CLUSTERS ARE FORECAST TO EVOLVE OFF OF THE TROUGH/DRYLINE...AND WILL POSE AN ISOLATED THREAT FOR DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND LARGE HAIL.

sections.title: SRN FL PENINSULA
sections.text: MEAN DEEP-LAYER FLOW WILL BE OUT OF THE E TODAY OVER THE SRN FL PENINSULA...AND WILL FOCUS ISOLATED TO SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ALONG THE W COAST BY AFTERNOON. MODERATE INSTABILITY IS FORECAST TO DEVELOP OVER THE AREA...AND GIVEN THE PRESENCE OF STEEPENING LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND PW VALUES IN EXCESS OF 1.7 INCHES...A FEW STORMS MAY POSE A MARGINAL SEVERE WEATHER THREAT. ..GARNER/MOSIER.. 06/21/2013

sections.title: WI/IA/IL
sections.text: A LONG-LIVED MCS IS TRACKING EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS IA/WI TOWARD LAKE MI. THIS SYSTEM HAS RESULTED IN SEVERAL REPORTS OF DAMAGING WINDS OVERNIGHT. ACTIVITY IS MOVING INTO AN INCREASINGLY MORE STABLE ENVIRONMENT...AND IS EXPECTED TO SLOWLY WEAKEN BY EARLY AFTERNOON. NEVERTHELESS...ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS PARTS OF IA/WI/IL.

sections.title: MN/IA/SD THROUGH THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: IN THE WAKE OF THE WI MCS...A WELL-DEFINED OUTFLOW BOUNDARY EXTENDS ACROSS NORTHERN IA INTO EASTERN SD. THIS BOUNDARY IS LIKELY TO LIFT SLOWLY NORTHWARD TODAY...ALLOWING VERY MOIST AND UNSTABLE AIR TO RETURN QUICKLY NORTHWARD INTO SD/MN. MODELS VARY ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF DAYTIME CONVECTION IN THIS REGION...BUT ANY STORMS THAT FORM WOULD HAVE A THREAT OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS.

sections.title: MT/SD THIS MORNING
sections.text: SATELLITE LOOPS SHOW A SUBTLE SHORTWAVE TROUGH ROTATING ACROSS THE NORTHERN ROCKIES INTO EASTERN MT/WY. THIS FEATURE HAS AIDED IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF SCATTERED MORNING THUNDERSTORMS OVER EASTERN MT AND WESTERN SD. THE 12Z RAP RAOB SHOWS STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND ONLY A WEAK CAP. THIS MAY ALLOW THE STRONGER STORMS THIS MORNING TO POSE A RISK OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS.

sections.title: HIGH PLAINS INTO DAKOTAS/MN TONIGHT
sections.text: LATER THIS EVENING...MODEL SOLUTIONS ARE IN BETTER AGREEMENT THAT SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS WILL DEVELOP ALONG AN AXIS FROM SOUTHEAST MT INTO WESTERN NEB. STEEP LOW/MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND STRONG HEATING WILL PROMOTE A RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL IN THE STRONGEST STORMS. DEEP LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR SUPERCELL STRUCTURES CAPABLE OF VERY LARGE HAIL AT TIMES. THIS ACTIVITY MAY GROW UPSCALE DURING THE EVENING AND TRACK ACROSS THE DAKOTAS INTO MN OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: WEST TX/EAST NM
sections.text: STRONG HEATING/DESTABILIZATION WILL LIKELY LEAD TO ANOTHER ROUND OF STRONG THUNDERSTORMS LATER TODAY OVER EASTERN NM AND WEST TX. SIMILAR TO YESTERDAY...THE STRONGEST CELLS WILL POSE A RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL FOR A FEW HOURS BEFORE WEAKENING AFTER SUNSET. ..HART/ROGERS.. 06/21/2013

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: BLOCKING LINGERS WITHIN THE LARGE-SCALE UPPER FLOW ACROSS THE EASTERN PACIFIC INTO THE WESTERN U.S...BUT THE BRITISH COLUMBIA HIGH CENTER MAY BEGIN TO WEAKEN...WHILE THE NORTHERN U.S. INTERMOUNTAIN REGION UPPER CLOSED LOW REDEVELOPS NORTHWARD INTO WEST CENTRAL CANADA. WITHIN LINGERING CYCLONIC FLOW ENCOMPASSING MUCH OF THE PACIFIC COAST THROUGH THE ROCKIES...THE MOST SIGNIFICANT SHORT WAVE IMPULSE APPEARS LIKELY TO GRADUALLY TURN EASTWARD THROUGH THE NORTHERN GREAT BASIN TODAY. THE TENDENCY FOR MID-LEVEL HEIGHTS TO RISE DOWNSTREAM OF THIS IMPULSE MAY TEMPER FALLS ACROSS THE NORTH CENTRAL PLAINS...BUT AN IMPULSE MIGRATING NORTHEASTWARD THROUGH THE NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS ALREADY IS CONTRIBUTING TO STRONG/SEVERE CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT ACROSS PARTS OF THE WESTERN AND CENTRAL DAKOTAS. MEANWHILE...A PRECEDING SHORT WAVE IMPULSE IS TURNING EASTWARD AROUND THE CREST OF BROADER SCALE UPPER RIDGING ACROSS THE GREAT LAKES REGION. AS THIS FEATURE CONTINUES EASTWARD INTO AND THROUGH A MORE STABLE ENVIRONMENT...THE LARGE MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM THAT IT SUPPORTED APPEARS LIKELY TO CONTINUE GRADUALLY WEAKENING TO ITS SOUTHWEST...ACROSS PARTS OF THE UPPER MIDWEST. WITHIN BROADER SCALE UPPER RIDGI

sections.title: NORTHERN AND CENTRAL PLAINS THROUGH UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY
sections.text: GIVEN CURRENT CONVECTIVE TRENDS...PRIMARY CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT MAY ALREADY BE UNDERWAY EAST OF THE BLACK HILLS...IN THE PRESENCE OF ENHANCED LOWER/MID TROPOSPHERIC WARM ADVECTION...ON THE NORTHERN FRINGE OF THE MORE STRONGLY CAPPING ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR PRESENT ACROSS MUCH OF THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN PLAINS. DEEP LAYER SHEAR IS STRONG ACROSS THIS REGION...ASSOCIATED WITH LOW-LEVEL EASTERLIES BENEATH MODEST SOUTHWESTERLY MID-LEVEL FLOW. AND THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES ARE CHARACTERIZED BY STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...AND RELATIVELY HIGH LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE CONTENT...SUPPORTING LARGE CAPE. THIS ENVIRONMENT PROBABLY WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF CONSIDERABLE UPSCALE GROWTH ACROSS CENTRAL AND EASTERN SOUTH DAKOTA INTO THE AFTERNOON HOURS. IN ADDITION TO THE RISK FOR LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WIND POTENTIAL IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE AS A MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM EVOLVES. MORE UNCERTAINTY LINGERS EAST OF THE MID MISSOURI VALLEY...BUT STRONGER ACTIVITY LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING MAY TEND TO DEVELOP SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS SOUTHERN MINNESOTA AND NORTHERN IOWA...ALONG/NORTH OF THE REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ASSOCIATED WITH WEAKENING STORM CLUSTER NOW OVER THE UPPER MIDWEST. MEANWHILE...ADDITIONAL STR

sections.title: SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: MID/UPPER FORCING FOR STORM DEVELOPMENT REMAINS UNCLEAR. HOWEVER...STRONG BOUNDARY LAYER HEATING AND MIXING TO CONVECTIVE TEMPERATURES APPEARS POSSIBLE AGAIN TODAY EAST OF THE SURFACE TROUGH TO THE LEE OF THE ROCKIES. AIDED BY LARGE SUB-CLOUD TEMPERATURE-DEW POINT SPREADS...AND THE DOWNWARD MIXING OF HIGHER MOMENTUM ASSOCIATED WITH A STRENGTHENING SOUTHERLY LOW-LEVEL JET ...ACTIVITY WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY THE RISK FOR SEVERE WIND GUSTS THIS EVENING. ..KERR/JIRAK.. 06/21/2013

sections.title: NORTH-CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS TO UPPER MIDWEST/UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: FORECAST SCENARIO REMAINS LARGELY UNCHANGED...SEE PRIOR DISCUSSION BELOW AND MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS. A SEVERE MCS/SOME PERIPHERAL SUPERCELLS WILL CONTINUE EASTWARD THIS AFTERNOON FROM EASTERN SD INTO SOUTHERN MN/ADJACENT NORTHWEST IA...WHILE OTHER/INITIALLY MORE DISCRETE STORMS INCREASE THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS THE NORTH-CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS. A SEVERE MCS MAY ULTIMATELY EVOLVE ACROSS WESTERN/NORTHERN NEB AND SOUTHERN SD TONIGHT...WITH A SEVERE WIND THREAT.

sections.title: SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: SOME SPATIAL ADJUSTMENTS MADE TO CATEGORICAL SLIGHT RISK ACROSS WEST TX...AND TO EXTEND LOW TSTM/CONDITIONAL WIND PROBABILITIES INTO MORE OF OK. FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION...SEE MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 1155. ..GUYER.. 06/21/2013 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1124 AM CDT FRI JUN 21 2013/

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS FOR THE SRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: ...N-CNTRL HIGH PLAINS INTO THE UPPER MS VALLEY/UPPER MIDWEST... A QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT IS LOCATED AT THE SURFACE FROM ERN WY SEWD INTO NERN CO...AND THEN NEWD INTO FAR SERN SD...WHERE IT THEN TRANSITIONS TO A WARM FRONT THAT EXTENDS EWD ALONG THE MN/IA BORDER BEFORE ARCING SWD INTO ERN IA. IN ADDITION...AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY PRODUCED BY A DECAYING MCS HAS BEEN LAID OUT OVER WRN/CNTRL IL EWD INTO CNTRL IND. TEMPERATURES IN THE 80S/90S AND DEWPOINTS FROM THE LOW 70S IN IA TO LOW 60S IN WRN/CNTRL NEB EXIST ALONG AND S OF THE STATIONARY AND WARM FRONTAL BOUNDARIES. THIS AIRMASS COMBINED WITH A PLUME OF STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES IS AIDING IN STRONG TO EXTREME INSTABILITY OVER THE WARM SECTOR. EARLY THIS EVENING...A FORWARD PROPAGATING MCS WAS MOVING EWD ACROSS CNTRL/SRN MN. CURRENT RADAR TRENDS INDICATE THIS ACTIVITY IS WEAKENING QUICKLY AND THE SEVERE THREAT HAS DIMINISHED SOMEWHAT IN THE SHORT-TERM. FARTHER WSW...THUNDERSTORM CLUSTERS...INCLUDING A FEW SUPERCELLS...HAVE DEVELOPED ALONG AND N OF THE STATIONARY FRONT OVER WRN NEB/NERN CO/ERN WY. ADDITIONAL STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL BE SUPPORTED NEWD ALONG THE STATIONARY FRONT BY FAVORABLE LOW-LEVEL WAA/FRONTOGENESIS OCCURRING IN TH

sections.title: SRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: SURFACE TROUGH/DRYLINE EXTENDS SSWWD FROM A LOW IN ERN CO THROUGH ERN NM INTO FAR W TX. ISOLATED STORMS HAVE EVOLVED OFF OF THIS BOUNDARY...POSSIBLY AIDED BY INCREASING LARGE-SCALE ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH AN UPPER IMPULSE RACING EWD ACROSS AZ/NM. MLCAPE VALUES FROM 1000-2000 J/KG...STEEP LAPSE RATES...AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR NEAR 40 KT WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT A LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING WIND THREAT INTO PART OF THE NIGHT BEFORE THE BOUNDARY LAYER STABILIZES WITH THE LOSS OF DAYTIME HEATING. ..GARNER.. 06/22/2013

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED STRONG-SVR STORMS ARE POSSIBLE ACROSS THE WRN DAKOTAS AND PARTS OF NERN WY AND SERN MT THIS MORNING. THE PRIMARY THREAT WILL BE LARGE HAIL...AND A LESSER THREAT FOR STRONG WIND GUSTS...AT LEAST THROUGH THE NEXT TWO HRS OR SO. DUE TO THE EXPECTED ISOLATED COVERAGE OF THE THREAT...A WW IS NOT CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: VISIBLE AND WATER VAPOR SATELLITE LOOPS SHOW RECENT DEVELOPMENT OF ISOLATED TSTMS ACROSS THE NRN HIGH PLAINS...LIKELY IN RESPONSE TO LOW-LEVEL WARM ADVECTION AND THE PRESENCE OF A SUBTLE UPPER IMPULSE ROTATING THROUGH BROAD CYCLONIC FLOW. THE 12Z RAP SOUNDING SAMPLED STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AND MODERATELY STRONG FLOW ALOFT. WITH A STABLE BOUNDARY LAYER IN PLACE...TSTMS ARE LIKELY ELEVATED...AND WILL POSE A PRIMARY THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL...ESPECIALLY IN ANY ORGANIZED CONVECTION. HOWEVER...DIURNAL HEATING OVER THE NEXT FEW HRS WILL RESULT IN FURTHER DESTABILIZATION...AND MAY SUPPORT A THREAT FOR STRONG-MARGINALLY SVR WIND GUSTS LATER THIS MORNING AS WELL. CURRENT THINKING IS THAT COVERAGE WILL REMAIN TOO ISOLATED FOR A WW TO BE NEEDED ATTM...BUT CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A NEW WW MAY BE NEEDED TO THE SOUTH OF WW 333 THIS MORNING AS A BOWING LINE OF STORMS IN SWRN WI TO FAR NERN IA TRACKS SEWD...REACHING FAR NRN IL AND PART OF EAST CENTRAL IA JUST AFTER 14Z. DAMAGING WIND THREAT MAY EXTEND INTO ERN WI...THOUGH A MORE STABLE ENVIRONMENT WITH NWD EXTENT COULD LIMIT THIS THREAT IN NERN WI. FARTHER W...ISOLATED HAIL REMAINS A THREAT IN PARTS OF NRN IA TO THE WEST OF WW 333.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 1245Z...MOSAIC RADAR IMAGERY SHOWED THE NRN EXTENT OF A BOWING LINE OF TSTMS...NOW APPROACHING ERN WI HAS BEGUN TO WEAKEN IN INTENSITY...THOUGH REMAINS MOVING EWD AT 40-45 KT. THE SRN EXTENT OF THIS LINE...NOW MOVING SEWD AT 40-45 KT THROUGH SWRN WI AND FAR NERN IA...COULD PERSIST A FEW MORE HOURS ACROSS SRN WI WITH A PORTION OF THE LINE MOVING INTO NRN IL/EAST CENTRAL IA JUST AFTER 14Z. ALTHOUGH AN INSTABILITY GRADIENT EXTENDED INTO ERN IA AND NRN IL...THE BOWING LINE WILL MOVE SOUTH OF STRONGER FLOW ALOFT THAT COULD LIMIT ITS FORWARD SPEED AND OVERALL SEVERE WEATHER THREAT SOUTH OF WW 333. MEANWHILE...THE NRN EXTENT OF THE LINE MOVING INTO EAST CENTRAL AND NERN WI SHOULD BECOME ELEVATED /OR MORE ELEVATED WITH TIME/ GIVEN A MORE STABLE ENVIRONMENT INTO THESE AREAS PER 12Z GRB SOUNDING. ADDITIONAL ELEVATED STORMS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE THIS MORNING ACROSS FAR NRN IA WITHIN A LOW LEVEL WAA REGIME ALONG AND NORTH OF A SWD MOVING OUTFLOW BOUNDARY. MODERATE INSTABILITY AND BULK SHEAR OF 35-40 KT REMAIN SUFFICIENT FOR ORGANIZED STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THREAT FOR MAINLY ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND WILL PERSIST FROM ERN IA INTO NRN IL NEXT FEW HOURS. STORMS MAY BEGIN TO AFFECT PORTIONS OF THE CHICAGO METRO BY 1630-17Z...AND DEPENDING ON CONVECTIVE TRENDS...ADDITIONAL COUNTIES IN NERN IL MIGHT NEED TO BE INCLUDED IN THE CURRENT WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LINEAR MCS FROM SERN WI THROUGH NWRN IL INTO ECNTRL IA CONTINUES SEWD AT AROUND 20 KT. THE LINE IS MOVING SOUTH OF STRONGER WINDS ALOFT...AND THIS AREA RESIDES EAST OF THE STEEPER MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES. HOWEVER...SFC TEMPERATURES ARE WARMING THROUGH THE LOW 80S SUPPORTING 1500-2000 J/KG MLCAPE. DESPITE THE POTENTIAL LIMITING FACTORS...SOME INTENSIFICATION IS POSSIBLE AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZES. ..DIAL.. 06/21/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: PRIMARY SHORT TERM SEVERE THREAT APPEARS TO BE WITH STORMS MOVING INTO JONES AND MELLETTE COUNTIES IN SCNTRL SD. THESE STORMS MAY POSE A THREAT FOR DAMAGING WIND AND LARGE HAIL NEXT COUPLE HOURS. OTHER STORMS DEVELOPING FARTHER NORTH AND NORTHWEST WILL POSE MAINLY A LARGE HAIL THREAT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SEVERE STORMS OVER SCNTRL SD CONTINUE TO EXHIBIT SEVERE WEATHER SIGNATURES INCLUDING A REAR INFLOW NOTCH AND LARGE MESH VALUES. THE STORM IS MOVING INTO AN ENVIRONMENT WHERE 700 MB TEMPERATURES ARE WARMER IMPLYING A POSSIBLE STRONGER CAP. HOWEVER...THE BOUNDARY LAYER IS WARMING AND DESTABILIZING WITH TEMPERATURES RISING INTO THE LOW-MID 80S SUPPORTING 2500-3000 J/KG MLCAPE. DESPITE WARMER DOWNSTREAM MID-LEVEL TEMPERATURES...ELY LOW LEVEL WINDS FROM THE DESTABILIZING WARM SECTOR AND SUPERCELL WIND PROFILES SUGGEST THIS STORM MAY PERSIST AS AN ORGANIZED SYSTEM NEXT COUPLE HOURS WITH BOTH BOWING AND SUPERCELL CHARACTERISTICS AS IT BECOMES SURFACE BASED WITH DAMAGING WIND AND LARGE HAIL LIKELY. OTHER STORMS DEVELOPING FARTHER NORTH ACROSS NWRN AND NRN SD SHOULD REMAIN ELEVATED ABOVE A STABLE BOUNDARY LAYER WITH LARGE HAIL THE MAIN THREAT. ..DIAL.. 06/21/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO DEVELOP THROUGH ECNTRL SD INTO SWRN MN THIS AFTERNOON INTO EARLY EVENING. PRIMARY THREATS ARE EXPECTED TO BE LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND...BUT ISOLATED TORNADOES CANNOT BE RULED OUT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CLUSTER OF STORMS CONTINUES EWD THROUGH ECNTRL AND NERN SD. LONG LIVED STORM CURRENTLY OVER BUFFALO COUNTY REMAINS SEVERE WITH BOWING STRUCTURES...WHILE OTHER STORMS ARE DEVELOPING ALONG WARM ADVECTION WING EAST OF THIS FEATURE. ACTIVITY WILL PROBABLY DEVELOP ENEWD FOR A WHILE AS THEY RIDE ALONG NRN FRINGE OF WARMER 700 MB TEMPERATURES BEFORE TURNING MORE EWD AND ESEWD. THE DOWNSTREAM ATMOSPHERE HAS BECOME STRONGLY UNSTABLE WITH 2500-3500 J/KG MLCAPE ALONG AND SOUTH OF A CONVECTIVELY ENHANCED FRONTAL BOUNDARY. THIS REGION RESIDES ON NOSE OF A STRENGTHENING SLY LLJ WITH HODOGRAPHS SUPPORTIVE OF LOW-LEVEL MESO-CYCLONES AND POSSIBLE TORNADOES. ORGANIZED STORMS WITH BOTH SUPERCELL AND BOWING STRUCTURES WILL LIKELY PERSIST WITHIN ZONE OF FORCING ACCOMPANYING THE EWD MOVING MCV.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP AND INTENSIFY FROM SERN WY INTO WRN NEB THIS AFTERNOON INTO THE EVENING. TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR A WW WHICH WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED BY 20-21Z. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND APPEAR LIKELY...BUT A COUPLE TORNADOES CANNOT BE RULED OUT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: HIGH BASED CONVECTION HAS DEVELOPED WITHIN THE DRY AND DEEPLY MIXED REGIME OVER SERN WY. CONVECTIVELY REINFORCED BOUNDARY EXTENDS FROM A SFC LOW IN NCNTRL NEB SWWD INTO SERN WY THEN NWWD THROUGH ERN WY. THE SFC LAYER HAS BEEN CLOUDY AND RELATIVELY STABLE ON COOL SIDE OF THIS BOUNDARY. HOWEVER...LOW CLOUDS ARE FINALLY MIXING OUT WITH TEMPERATURES WARMING TO THE LOW 80S WITHIN MOIST SFC LAYER NORTH OF THE BOUNDARY SUPPORTING 2000-2500 J/KG MLCAPE. HIGH BASED STORMS MAY INTENSIFY AS THEY MOVE EWD INTO THE MOIST AND UNSTABLE REGIME. OTHER STORMS MAY INITIATE ALONG THE BOUNDARY OVER WRN NEB. THIS REGION RESIDES ALONG THE SRN PERIPHERY OF STRONGER SWLY WINDS ALOFT WITH 40+ KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS. THE MAIN THREATS WILL BE LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS...BUT A COUPLE TORNADOES CANNOT BE RULED OUT WHERE STORMS INTERACT WITH THE MODIFYING BOUNDARY.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SCTD SVR TSTMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP IN THE 20Z TO 23Z TIME FRAME WITH THE THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL. STORM MERGERS MAY LEAD TO E/SEWD MOVING CLUSTERS WITH A CONTINUED SVR WIND THREAT THROUGH EARLY EVENING. CONVECTIVE TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR THE POSSIBILITY OF AN INCREASING SVR THREAT THAT COULD REQUIRE A WW IN THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS.

AND MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY /MLCAPE AROUND 2500 J PER KG PER SPC MESOANALYSIS/.
